newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 7.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
-- PRESSURE MOUNTS ON BONN FOR 'CONTROLLED' EMU DELAY

Pressure is mounting on the Bonn government to delay the onset of EMU, as Bavarian prime minister Edmund Stoiber and a member of Germany's Christian Social Union have called, in an interview with the Financial Times, for a 'controlled' euro delay. The two officials believe strict adherence to Maastricht criteria would provide greater advantages than proceeding with a weak euro. Social Democrat pri me minister Gerhard Schroder also backed a delay if cuts required to meet entry criteria were 'too painful', while deputy leader of the German trade federation, Ursula Engelen-Kefer, has warned that unions will pull out of their EMU backing if EMU entry will require further welfare cuts.
-- LIB DEMS ACCUSE BROWN OF HIDING 5 BLN STG SPENDING CUT

Chancellor Gordon Brown has been accused by the Liberal Democrat party of hiding in his Budget a five billion stg real-term cut in public spending which holds potential for 'devastating' effects on jobs and services. The cut, confirmed by House of Commons researchers, stems from expectations of increases in public sector inflation which will erode the actual value of public spending. Members of the Liberal Democrat party accuse Brown of making a 'windfall gain' by increasing tax revenue forecasts to reflect higher inflation without increasing spending totals.
-- ONLINE MARKET SET UP TO TRADE TELEPHONE TIME

Furthering the liberalisation of Britain's telecommunications market, a new electronic trading exchange for 'telephone minutes' is to be launched in the UK this week. Band-X, which operates through the Internet, permits the 150 licensed carriers in the UK to buy and sell capacity on long-distance telephone lines. If successful, such an electronic market could improve efficiency in the telecoms market by taking the place of faxes and telephone calls through which sellers distribute prices to potential buyers.
-- INDUSTRY 'TOO LATE' TO RESOLVE COMPUTER TIME-BOMB

Geoff Unwin, chief operating officer at computer services company Cap Gemini, has expressed growing concern that businesses and government are failing to take the millennium bug problem seriously. Unwin calculated that even if all available resources were pooled into solving the problem, they would still be insufficient to meet the deadline, as even 'Cap Gemini is having problems recruiting enough staff'. Unwin has now proposed a campaign which if necessary would include legislation, to increase awareness of issues surrounding the Year 2000 problem.
-- BBC MAY ASK FOR INCREASE IN LICENCE FEE

BBC director-general John Birt is expected to make a request to the government to reconsider its five-year licence fee arrangement and grant the group additional funding to assist it in the move to digital broadcasting and to help it deal with increased competition. Gavyn Davies, Goldman Sachs' chief international economic adviser and Andrew Graham, an economics tutor at Balliol College in Oxford, have predicted the BBC faces long-term decline unless finances are boosted.
-- BANK POISED FOR QUARTER-POINT RATE RISE

Economists City-wide believe that the monetary committee at the Bank of England's monetary policy committee will raise interest rates from 6.5 percent to 6.75 percent in an attempt to restrain consumer spending. If a quarter-point rise were to take place, it would be the third quarter-point rise in three months and if a half-point rise takes place, base rates will be at their highest since early 1993. Short-sterling futures contracts are predicting base rates of seven percent by September.
-- CHANNEL 5 'IN NEED OF FUNDS' FOR PROGRAMMES

Top executives at Channel 5, Britain's fifth terrestrial station partly owned by the Pearson media group, are looking at new investment in programming in an attempt to lift audience figures to its goal of five percent of total viewing by the end of the year. One Channel 5 senior executive has predicted the company will need to invest as much as 50 million stg to make any impact. Latest viewing figures show Channel 5 with a 2.9 percent share, figures which are rising very slowly.
-- RETAILERS FAIL TO MEET CUSTOMERS' EXPECTATIONS

A recent Gallup poll commissioned by consultancy and training group Forum Europe and conducted in the UK reveals one in three consumers cannot name a single company which they believe delivers excellent service. Jennifer Potter-Brotman of Forum Europe commented that 'consumer expectations are growing...a lot faster than companies are responding' and recommended that companies should now invest in finding out who their valuable customers were, what they wanted and what would 'delight them' or set them apart from the rest of the field.
-- HUNT FOR NEW CHIEF EXECUTIVE BEGINS AT WH SMITH

Four non-executive directors of WH Smith will meet on Monday morning to discuss possible candidates to replace chief executive Bill Cockburn who announced his resignation two weeks ago. The company is undergoing a period of turmoil and one director has admitted it is 'running far behind in the retail business and is not where it should be'. The list of candidates to replace Cockburn is said to be filled with external candidates, most of whom are UK retailers.
-- VODAFONE CHANGES CORPORATE IDENTITY

Leading UK mobile operator Vodafone is in the final stage of preparations for the Monday announcement of a near-complete overhaul of its corporate identity. As part of the make-over, its 300 high street stores will get a 'facelift', many separate brands will be cut, a unified billing system will be introduced and its distribution business will be restructured. The changes are being made in an attempt to solidify Vodafone's leading market position and to help stimulate sluggish growth.
